notes: Attacks and spells have effects: sparks when weapons hit, bursts of each school's colour when spells land, sparkles on heals, rings rising on buffs, and creatures' bolts flying to their targets.
Casters' hands glow in their spell's colour while casting.
Cloaks are cloth: they trail, ripple and flap as you run and swing round when you turn.
Movement is smoother: characters and the camera no longer stutter, whatever your frame rate.
Corpses you've already looted no longer block clicks on the ones under them.
The Options window can be moved by dragging its title, and stays where you put it.
Every creature now has a real model: wolves, boars, the forest bear and spiders run, bite and fall, and burrowlings, mirefin and the Ditchjaw gnolls carry their own weapons.
Two-handed weapons, staves and polearms are held in both hands in a fight, with a second swing and two-handed parries.
The target ring now lies on the ground under your target, the whole circle showing on slopes and steps, sized to your target and easier to spot from far away.
Smoother with lots of playerbots around: name labels, quest markers and distant characters cost much less.
Spellswords start with a two-handed sword, the Initiate's Greatsword.

Ranged attacks: the new Shoot ability (in your spellbook) fires your bow, gun, throwing weapon or wand at your target again and again until you stop. Stand still to shoot. Bows, guns and throwing weapons can't hit targets closer than 8 yards; wands can.
Wands deal damage of their own type and can be resisted. Cleric playerbots holding a wand use it once they run low on mana.
New playable races: Dwarves (Man-at-Arms, Templar, Cleric) and Gnomes (Man-at-Arms), with their own models and looks to choose. Playerbots can be Dwarves and Gnomes too.
Helms and cloaks now show on your character: hoods, caps, mail coifs and plate helms by armour type.
Brigands, their hedge-mages and Odo the Collector now look like people, in red hoods with their weapons.
Your bow, gun or throwing knife comes out while you shoot, with aiming and shooting animations.
Everything that stacks now stacks to 20.
Arrows and shot are gone: ranged weapons need no ammo. Throwing knives and axes are now single weapons, bought one at a time.

New class: the Spellsword, a fighter who inscribes Edges of flame, frost, storm or warding on their blade and releases the Resonance their hits build. Tank in Wardweave Form or deal damage in Bladesong Form. Train with Magister Ilsabet Rhee in the priory or Tamsin Vey in Wexford.

Humans now have real 3D models, male and female, with animations for walking, running, strafing, jumping, sitting, attacking, blocking, casting, getting hit, being stunned, dying and emotes (/wave, /bow, /cheer, /laugh, /cry, /dance, /thank).
Your weapon and shield show in your hands, and your armour's colours show on your character.
Choose your body, skin, hair, hair colour and beard when making a Human character.
Human playerbots and townsfolk use the new models too, dressed for their trade.
Party bar: set a party member's role (Tank, Healer or Damage). They respec their talents and fight to match.

For now, new characters and playerbots can only be Humans of the classes with spells (Man-at-Arms, Templar, Cleric and Spellsword). Other races and classes return when they're finished; characters you already made still play.
Playerbots outside your party leave the creatures and chests your quests need to you.
Passive abilities such as Parry no longer go on your action bar, and say Passive in the spellbook.
Deleting a character accepts "delete" in any case, and Enter confirms.
The frame rate counter now sits in the top right corner.
Fixed Esc not opening the main menu.

Party Commands is now a bar of icons above the menu buttons, like a pet bar, instead of a window whose buttons overlapped. Pick a party member (or Everyone) by their portrait, then give orders; each buff slot shows the spell they keep up, and clicking it shows the choices.
A party member's bags now open beside your own.
Party Commands (K, or the new button beside the action bar): a small window you can keep open while you play, to give orders to the playerbots in your party.
Tell each member to follow or stay, attack your target, and whether to assist you, defend the party or stay passive.
Send members to sell their junk or everything in their bags to a vendor near you, or to their trainer to learn new spells.
Choose the buffs each member keeps up: a Templar's Presence, Oath and Boon, a Cleric's Fortitude, Spirit, Warding and own buffs, a Man-at-Arms' stance and shout.
Open a member's bags to give and take items freely, soulbound ones included, and to put gear on them.
Party members now learn new spells only when you take them to their trainer, paying from their own money and yours. They'll tell you when they have something to learn.
Playerbots find their way round houses, fences, walls, trees and rocks instead of getting stuck on them.
Creatures come back twice as fast.
Key bindings can use Shift, Ctrl and Alt with a key, such as Shift-1.
The game also checks for updates when you return to the menu from the game.

The world map (M) now shows every quest giver with a quest for you, and where to go for the quests you're on: where the creatures you need live, places to explore and chests holding what you need. Hover any of them to see what it is.
The minimap only shows quests to take when they're close enough to be on it, so it stays tidy. Quests to turn in still point the way from its edge.
The game now checks for updates when it starts. When a new version is out, choose Update to download and install it, and the game starts again on its own.
Not now? Choose Later to be asked next time, or Skip This Version.
A new Interface option, Check for Updates at Start, turns the check off.
Fixed a white box showing behind an item while you carry it from your bags.
Adventurers in Harrowfield now give directions from Wexford, not the priory.
Ask an adventurer who gives a quest and they'll say where that person really stands.
Ask about a trainer and you're pointed to the nearest one of that class, in Wexford or the priory.
A whole new look: every window, frame, button and tab now shares one dark, gold-trimmed style, with titles in a carved serif.
Painted icons for every spell and item, on the action bars, in the spellbook, bags, character window, loot, vendors, quest rewards, trades, buffs and talents.
Your frame, your target's and your party's now show portraits: your class's emblem, or the kind of creature you're facing.
Health, mana and experience bars sit in gold-edged troughs, and your target's frame keeps its size whether or not it has mana.
Talents show their icons, glow gold when you can put a point in, and keep their rank in a small badge.
A second zone: Harrowfield, farmland for levels 6 to 12 over the mountain pass south of Ashford Vale, many times the size of the vale.
Harrowfield's village, Wexford, has an inn, a chapel and churchyard, a smithy, trainers for Templars, Clerics and Men-at-Arms, and Hesketh Steele the weaponsmith.

Explore the Coombe farm and its pumpkin patch, the Old Delve and Copperhollow mines, the Mirrow Mere and its mirefin village, Thornwick Tower, the Ashwood lumber camp, the Pellow vineyard, the Reedford landing, the west garrison, a brigand farmstead and the gnoll hills.
Twenty-nine quests in Harrowfield, among them the search for the lost watchmen, the hunt for the Collector, and Grunmaw.
New kinds of quest: explore a place, gather things lying in the world such as Bundles of Wood, and start a quest from an item you find. Some quests begin and end at things rather than people.
New creatures: mirefins, flintback boars, prowlers, young forest bears, Ditchjaw gnolls, brigand cutthroats and hedge-mages, and more. Spiders' bites poison, and gnoll outriders strike twice.
Godric Vane, the Weapon Master by the priory, teaches weapon skills.
A world map: press M to see your zone, your party and where you stand, or pick the whole world.
Menu buttons beside the action bar for Character Info, Spellbook, Talents, Quest Log, Socials, World Map and the Main Menu.
Playerbots travel between zones through the pass and quest in Harrowfield too.
Whisper a playerbot about the item it's selling to get its price. Trades with a playerbot start with the item you talked about already in.
Buffs others cast on you and your party's playerbots are kept when you log out and back in.
The game runs smoothly with many more playerbots, and the Random Bots option now goes up to 400.
Tooltips fit their text, and near the bottom of the screen they appear above the cursor.
Behind-the-scenes testing tools only: nothing changes in play.
Creatures call for help: pull a brigand and its friends close by join in a moment later, and their pulls can bring more.
Some creatures now speak when they attack you. Their words show in the chat under Creature Speech.
Trainers have a Train All button that teaches everything you can afford.
The spellbook is laid out as in the old days: pages of twelve spells, with tabs down its right side for General and each talent tree. It opens under your portrait.
The spellbook has a Hide old ranks box, to show only the highest rank of each spell.
Your target's buffs and debuffs show under its frame. Hover over one to see what it does.
Templars: Boons and Greater Boons buttons in the spellbook open a menu of every boon you know. Put them on your action bar.
Class buffs that lasted 5 minutes or more now last an hour: Boons, Greater Boons, Litany of Fortitude, Uplifted Spirit, Inner Flame, Shadow Warding and more.
Boon icons show the boon's own name, so Boon of Strength and Boon of Shelter look different.
Playerbots treat grey items as junk: they won't try to sell them to you, and they sell them to vendors they pass.
Fixed talent rank numbers drawing over the talent tooltip.
Fixed tooltips getting in the way of the right action bars.
Long patch notes on the login screen now have a scroll bar.
Talents: from level 10 you earn a talent point each level, to spend in your class's three trees. Press N to open the talent window.
Men-at-Arms have Blademastery, Ferocity and Bulwark; Templars Grace, Aegis and Zeal; Clerics Devotion, Mercy and Umbra.
Abilities like Final Stand, Radiant Jolt and Hush now come from talents rather than the trainer. If you bought them before, spend your points to get them back.
Templars have three new talent abilities: Heaven's Favor, Hallowed Presence and Contrition.
Your class trainer can unlearn your talents, for a fee that rises each time.
Playerbots spend their talent points too.
Roots now hold players, playerbots and creatures in place.
Patch note dates are now written month-day-year.
The login screen now shows the notes for the latest patch.
The game now has a version number, shown on the login screen.
Creatures cast spells: Burrowling Firecallers throw Flame Bolts from range, Pickmen pry at your armor, Brigand Footpads stab from behind and Ridgetusk Boars charge.
Interrupt a casting creature with Hilt Strike, Shield Smash, Hush, stuns or fear. The target frame shows what your target is casting.
Stances show in your buffs, the active one is framed in gold, and clicking it again no longer gives an error.
Templars learn Revival's first rank free at level 12, so its higher ranks can be trained.
The Options window is one size, and long pages scroll.
